newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BOKSIC AND DEL PIERO SHINE AS JUVENTUS WIN 5-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOKSIC AND DEL PIERO SHINE AS JUVENTUS WIN 5-0.

text.p: Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero scored two goals each as holders Juventus toughened up their act and hammered Rapid Vienna 5-0 in a Champions' League group C match on Wednesday.
"We're looking good in every sense and we also got angry after the draw in Rome," said coach Marcello Lippi who experimented with a new attacking line-up.
"When Juve play like that, its hard for all other teams."
Juventus have been giving away late goals in recent matches. They drew 1-1 with Roma in serie A last weekend after conceding a goal deep into injury time.
Rapid held Juventus to a 1-1 draw in the home leg with a late goal and Juventus were fired up for revenge.
The 5-0 win -- one of the Turin team's best in the European Cup -- left unbeaten Juventus top of group C with 10 points and two matches left to play.
However, they are not yet mathematically assured of going through as one of the top two finishers.
Boksic put the Italian league leaders ahead after just four minutes on a drizzly night in Turin and grabbed his second -- and Juve's fourth -- in the 59th minute.
The Croat striker, fed by a header from defender Ciro Ferrara, twisted deftly in the area and slotted the ball neatly past two defenders and in at the near post.
Uruguayan Paolo Montero made it 2-0 in the 27th minute, rising in the box and heading in a free kick by French international Zinedine Zidane.

Italian international Del Piero, returning to the competition after a long injury layoff and playing in an attacking trio with Boksic and Zidane, stunned the Austrians a minute later with a virtuoso goal.
The 21-year-old ran almost half the length of the pitch, sidestepped goalkeeper Michael Konsel and scored.
Boksic made it 4-0 after being set up by Del Piero but the Croat was given no chance of a hat-trick. Lippi pulled him off in the 62nd minute.
Del Piero completed the rout in the 74th minute.
The Austrians, without injured Polish striker Andzrej Lesiak, rarely threatened the Juventus goal.

Juventus - 1-Angelo Peruzzi; 3-Moreno Torricelli, 4-Paolo Montero, 2-Ciro Ferrara, 22-Gianluca Pessotto (5-Sergio Porrini, 71st), 7-Angelo Di Livio (19-Attilio Lombardo, 62), 18-Vladimir Jugovic, 14-Didier Deschamps, 21-Zinedine Zidane, 9-Alen Boksic (11-Michele Padovano, 62), 10-Alessandro del Piero.

Rapid Vienna - 1-Michael Konsel, 4-Trifon Ivanov, 5-Peter Schoettel, 6-Peter Stoeger (Roman Pivarnik, 65), 7-Christian Stumpf (16-Krizystof Ratajczyk, 46th), 9-Marek Penksa (2-Prvoslav Jovanovic, 46), 10-Didi Kuhbauer, 11-Christian Prosenik, 18-Sergei Mandreko 19-Thomas Zingler, 20-Andreas Heraf.
